To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the parallel adaptive solution algorithm is robust for solving complex reacting flows; (ii) the adaptive mesh refinement algorithm is effective for resolving complex flow structures; (iii) the parallel adaptive mesh refinement approach is effective for predicting complex turbulent non-premixing combusting flows.

a parallel solution-adaptive approach for turbulent non-premixed combustion can predict the flow field and flame shape with reasonable accuracy and that the parallel adaptive approach is capable of predicting complex turbulent non-pre mixed combustion phenomena with high accuracy.
a parallel adaptive mesh refinement approach is a promising approach for the prediction of turbulent reacting flows.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of numerical algorithms and parallel software tools for the simulation of complex turbulent reacting flows in three-dimensional space.
the development and application of parallel adaptive solution algorithms to three-dimensional turbulent nonpremixed combusting flows.
the development of a new generation of parallel solution-adaptive methods for predicting three-dimensional turbulent reacting flows in complex geometries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the parallel AMR method is capable of predicting the complex three-dimensional flow features of turbulent non-premixed combustion with a level of fidelity not achievable using conventional structured or unstructured grid approaches.
the parallel adaptive mesh refinement approach is an effective tool for the prediction of three-dimensional non-premixed combusing flows.
the numerical results presented here demonstrate the validity of the parallel AMRI approach for predicting fine scale features of complex turbulent diffusion flames.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the parallel adaptive mesh refinement method is a powerful approach for the solution of turbulent combustion problems, and that the method is particularly useful for the solution of complex problems with large spatial variations in the solution field, and/or with complex geometries.
a parallel AMR approach is a viable approach for solving complex turbulent non-premixing combusting flows.
we have developed a parallel solution-adaptive method for three-dimensional combusting flows that can be used to predict fine-scale turbulent combustion features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parallel AMR is a promising approach for the prediction of complex turbulent combusting flows.
the parallel AMR algorithm can be used to predict complex three-dimensional combusting flows at a fraction of the computational cost of a comparable grid-based calculation.
the AMR method is capable of providing a solution that is both accurate and efficient for a wide range of flow conditions.
